paragraphs.title: Praise for God and the Limits of Human Reliance

answers: The son of man
The LORD
The princes
easy.explanation: The psalm begins, “Praise ye the LORD, O my soul.”
easy.q: Whom does the psalmist command his soul to praise?

answers: While he lives
Only in trouble
For one day
easy.explanation: He says, “While I live will I praise the LORD.”
easy.q: How long does the psalmist say he will praise the LORD?

answers: The LORD
Princes and the son of man
The God of Jacob
easy.explanation: The psalm says, “Put not your trust in princes, nor in the son of man.”
easy.q: In whom should people not put their trust?

answers: Aid or deliverance
A song of praise
A human thought
medium.explanation: The verse teaches that human rulers cannot provide unfailing aid or deliverance.
medium.q: In verse 3, what does “help” mean in the phrase “in whom there is no help”?

answers: They cannot speak
They die, and their thoughts perish
They cannot praise God
medium.explanation: When a person’s breath departs and he returns to the earth, his thoughts perish.
medium.q: Why should people not rely completely on human rulers?

answers: Praise to God, a lifelong commitment, a warning about human trust, and human mortality
Creation, judgment, kingship, and praise
Hunger, freedom, protection, and kingship
medium.explanation: These are the main ideas presented in order in the opening four verses.
medium.q: What is the order of ideas in verses 1–4?

answers: The LORD is worthy of praise, while human beings are not a lasting source of trust
The LORD lives briefly, while human beings live forever
The LORD needs help, while human beings create the world
challenge.explanation: The psalm joins praise for the eternal LORD with a warning about human weakness and mortality.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast between the LORD and human beings in this passage?

answers: Praise is a continuing commitment of the psalmist
Praise is spoken only once
Praise is meant only for human rulers
challenge.explanation: The psalmist promises to praise God while he lives and has any being.
challenge.q: What does the repetition of praise at the beginning suggest?

answers: It shows that even human thoughts and plans come to an end
It shows that man becomes the creator
It shows that man keeps truth forever
challenge.explanation: When a person returns to the earth, his thoughts perish with him.
challenge.q: How does the description of human death strengthen the warning not to trust in man?

answers: The person whose hope is in the LORD his God
The person who trusts in princes
The oppressed person only
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Happy is he that hath the God of Jacob for his help, whose hope is in the LORD.”
easy.q: Who is blessed according to verse 5?

answers: Only the earth
Heaven, earth, the sea, and all that is in them
Only the sea
easy.explanation: The LORD made heaven, earth, the sea, and all that therein is.

answers: The hungry
The princes
The wicked
easy.explanation: The psalm says that the LORD gives food to the hungry.
easy.q: To whom does the LORD give food?

answers: People who have been treated unjustly
People who sing praises
People who created the heavens
medium.explanation: The oppressed are those who suffer wrong or unjust treatment.

answers: The One who made the world also cares for people in need
The Creator does not care about the world
Creation prevents God from judging rightly
medium.explanation: After describing creation, the psalm lists God’s acts of justice, provision, release, and healing.
medium.q: How do the verses connect God’s work as Creator with His work as Deliverer?

answers: Preserving strangers
Loosing the prisoners
Turning the way of the wicked upside down
medium.explanation: The sequence includes judgment, food for the hungry, and loosing prisoners before the next verse’s acts.
medium.q: Which action appears before opening the eyes of the blind and raising those bowed down?

answers: It includes justice, provision, freedom, and care for the weak
It is limited to creating the world
It is offered only to the strong
challenge.explanation: The LORD judges for the oppressed, feeds the hungry, releases prisoners, opens blind eyes, and raises the bowed down.
challenge.q: What does the list of God’s actions show about the nature of His help?

answers: The LORD creates, keeps truth, and acts for those who need help
Human beings never die
There is no hunger or oppression in the world
challenge.explanation: The passage presents the LORD as the faithful Creator and helper of the needy.
challenge.q: Why is the person whose hope is in the LORD called happy?

answers: God’s faithfulness is shown through His just and merciful deeds
It means that God does not act in the world
It refers only to the sea
challenge.explanation: God’s enduring truth is demonstrated by His reliable care, justice, and deliverance.
challenge.q: How is “keepeth truth for ever” connected with the actions in the following verses?

paragraphs.title: Protection of the Vulnerable and God’s Eternal Kingship

answers: Strangers
The wicked only
Princes only
easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “The LORD preserveth the strangers.”

answers: The fatherless and widow
The sea and the earth
Human thoughts
easy.explanation: The verse says that the LORD relieves the fatherless and widow.

answers: For one day
For ever, throughout all generations
Until a man dies
easy.explanation: The LORD shall reign for ever, even unto all generations.
easy.q: How long shall the LORD reign?

answers: Makes crooked or overturns
Preserves and relieves
Gives food to
medium.explanation: The phrase describes God’s judgment against the path of the wicked.
medium.q: In the phrase “the way of the wicked he turneth upside down,” what does “turneth upside down” mean?

answers: He preserves and relieves the vulnerable, but overturns the way of the wicked
He punishes the vulnerable and helps the wicked
He ignores both groups
medium.explanation: Verse 9 contrasts God’s care for strangers, the fatherless, and the widow with His judgment on the wicked.
medium.q: What does the LORD do for the vulnerable, and what does He do to the wicked?

answers: With a declaration of His eternal reign and a call to praise
With a description of human death
With a description of the creation of the sea
medium.explanation: The final verse declares the LORD’s everlasting reign and ends with “Praise ye the LORD.”
medium.q: How does the psalm conclude after describing the LORD’s actions?

answers: His kingship is shown as a reign of protection, justice, and mercy
His kingship means that He gives up judging
His kingship concerns only one earthly place
challenge.explanation: The psalm presents God’s reign through His care for strangers, orphans, and widows.
challenge.q: What is the connection between the LORD’s care for the vulnerable and His kingship?

answers: The LORD’s reign continues from generation to generation
The LORD reigns for only one generation
The LORD’s reign belongs only to the past
challenge.explanation: The expression stresses the continuing and lasting nature of God’s kingship.

answers: The psalm has shown the LORD to be protector, judge, helper, and eternal King
The psalm focuses only on human weakness
The psalm is mainly about the creation of the sea
challenge.explanation: After describing God’s faithfulness, mercy, justice, and everlasting reign, the psalm calls for praise.
challenge.q: Why is the closing command, “Praise ye the LORD,” appropriate?
